articles.title: Middlesbrough 2-1 Swansea City: Will Lankshear steers Boro back to the top of the Championship
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Middlesbrough and Swansea City at the Riverside Stadium on Tuesday night; Will Lankshear returned to the starting line-up with the winning goal to send Boro back to the top of the table.
articles.body:
Lankshear had missed the final two games prior to the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Saturday's win over Bristol City.

Having been restored to the starting line-up at the Riverside, the Championship's leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to reestablish his side's lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku's driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris' opener.

Lankshear's winner came nine minutes into the second half, but the England Under-21 international was also heavily involved in the slick passing move that led to Boro opening the scoring in the ninth minute.

Lankshear's first-time pass released Neto Borges into the left of the area and when he squared across the face of the box, Peart-Harris slotted home a first-time strike of his own to claim his first goal since joining Middlesbrough in the summer.

Boro's lead lasted 13 minutes, with Swansea levelling when Lankshear was at fault at the opposite end of the field.

The striker bundled over Elijah Just on the edge of the area to concede a free-kick. Ben Cabango's goalbound header was nodded off the line by Ashley Phillips, but the ball broke to Opoku, who drilled home an excellent low finish from the edge of the area.

Boro went close to regaining their lead when Riley McGree fired a first-time strike just wide from a corner, and threatened again just before the interval when Peart-Harris volleyed over at the back post after David Strelec flicked Borges' cross into his path.

Swansea remained a threat though, and six minutes into the second half Adilson Malanda played Eom Ji-sung onside as Opoku's through ball unpicked the Boro defence, only for goalkeeper Radek Vitek to burst from his line to keep out the midfielder's shot with his foot.

It was a crucial save as just three minutes later Boro were scoring their second goal at the other end. Callum Brittain's pass sent Peart-Harris breaking away down the right, and when he squared the ball across the face of goal Lankshear was left with the easy task of tapping home.

Sebastian Berhalter should have added a third goal with 18 minutes remaining, but after coming off the bench the American midfielder dragged a shot wide from the right of the area.

His fellow replacement, Max Arfsten, also wasted a good late opportunity, drilling a low strike straight at goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux.

"I'm very happy. It's been a good week, with two wins from two tough games in different ways. We played two good sides, who make it difficult for you, and I'm happy to have come away with six points, six well-deserved points.

"If you look at the Bristol City game, then I think it's difficult to be free-flowing against 10 men in their own box with no intent of putting any pace in the game. I think it's difficult for any teams in the world when it becomes like that. It becomes about winning, and we did.

"This game was a little bit more back and forth. We created a lot of chances and should have scored four or five goals, but overall I'm very happy."

"I'm happy with the players. I'm pleased with the way they've applied themselves in the last two games, that's been second to none. The application has been excellent, listening to what we've been trying to do and then executing it.

"I think we can be better in possession, and if there's a disappointing thing, it's that. I think we're a better team than we're showing in possession.

"Middlesbrough are a good team. They make it difficult for you and put you in awkward positions when they have the ball, then when the ball turns over, I think that's something we could do a little bit better and where we have to get better at.

"I think we made it uncomfortable for Middlesbrough at times, and are probably disappointed not to get something out of the game. But there's lots of things we can learn from and improve on."

articles.title: Sheffield United 1-1 Southampton: Sydie Peck strikes again to earn point for Blades
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Sheffield United and Southampton at Bramall Lane on Tuesday night; Sydie Peck scores again as the Blades hit back to earn a point and cancel out Lewis Dobbins opener.
articles.body:
Lewis Dobbin had given the visitors an early lead but the Blades stepped up a gear after the break and finally found a way past Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz through Peck.

The equaliser saw the Blades move within a point of the top eight and remain two behind their sixth-placed opponents.

United have lost just once in their last seven games while Southampton have only suffered one defeat in their last nine outings.

Southampton struck in the 10th minute when Dobbin cut inside from the left wing and fired into the far corner of Michael Cooper's net.

Shortly after, Dobbin tested Cooper with a shot from 25 yards as the Saints pushed for a second.

United's solitary first-half effort on goal came from Romelle Donovan, whose angled shot was comfortably dealt with by Daniel Peretz.

United were lacklustre in the opening period as they missed loanee Ben Brereton-Diaz, who scored twice at the weekend but was unable to face his parent club.

In a bid to strengthen his side's firepower, manager Chris Wilder introduced Patrick Bamford at the start of the second half with Tom Cannon making way.

It did not take long for Bamford to have his first chance, putting a close-range header over after Peck's corner had been headed towards goal by Mark McGuinness.

Peretz had to keep out a near-post header from Jordan Ayew as the hosts looked to capitalise on their improved second-half performance.

The Southampton keeper was also called into action to thwart Harrison Burrows, Tahith Chong and Peck. The pick of his saves was when he flung himself to his right to keep out Chong's shot while Peck was disappointed to head straight at Peretz.

Southampton's resistance was finally broken in the final minute of the game when Ayew wriggled past his marker on the right byline and pulled the ball back to Peck, who slotted beyond Peretz for his fifth goal in four games.

Substitute Samuel Edozie spurned a great chance to score a winner for Southampton in added time. He was put through on goal by Finn Azaz and looked certain to score but Cooper stuck out a leg to divert the ball wide.

A Southampton winner would have been very harsh on the Blades who deserved at least a point from the game after dominating the second period.

"It was after 25 minutes of the first half. You know, they've come with a different shape, they've got really technical players.

"We didn't get to grips with their shape, they had control of the game, really technical, possession-based players. Seven touches in our box, first half.

"We had to get to grips with their press, our press, which we did after half an hour and started to get a foothold in the game and wrestle back a little bit of momentum because, yeah, they were on top.

"So we said to the players, 'need to be brave, need to wrestle this back. Game's not done, we're not three or four down, we're not out of sight, and we need to just be a little bit better in possession, get that press right', which we did.

"And the ball came back to us, and then off we went, started creating opportunities, being really positive, driving.

"I think it would have been the cruellest of cruel blows if they'd have nicked a winner. And I think we definitely deserve something from the game with the attitude and the way we played, and how brave we were."

"As I can remember, it's been one of the best first halves that we've had away from home in a long, long time.

"I think it's a very good start into the season, I think, in a long, long time. So I think very good start into the game. Went up on a great finish from Lewis. And I think throughout the first half, he had complete control.

"And then it is what it is. Like these games, they need a second goal at one point. I think we had the chance to score one in the first half. Then we went into half-time and we knew that the game is going to be completely different.

"For me, in the second half, it's the same thing. If you don't score a second one, then the game is just open until the very end.

"Then you need to bring it over the line, and we didn't manage to do that today.

"I think the game today needed a second goal from us, and we had the chance when we were up, we had the chance when we were drawing."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Bristol City 1-1 Wrexham: Cameron Pring earns point for Robins
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Bristol City and Wrexham at Ashton Gate on Tuesday night; Robins hit back for a point with improved performance after the break as Cameron Pring nets equaliser.
articles.body:
City boss Michael Skubala had to endure chants about his employment prospects from the Ashton Gate faithful after Joe Worrall had given Wrexham a seventh-minute lead.

But City - who had lost their previous four home games - lifted mounting pressure on Skubala with a spirited display that took them up two places to 16th in the Sky Bet Championship.

Cameron Pring rewarded the Robins' endeavour with a rare goal after 51 minutes, the full-back on target for the first time since December 2023.

Wrexham are now unbeaten in four games, but they stay 14th and may well consider this an opportunity lost after making such a strong start.

City fans screamed in vain for a stoppage-time penalty after Danny Imray had nudged over Scott Twine just inside the box.

Wrexham had not won at Ashton Gate since 1981 and its status as an unhappy hunting ground for the Red Dragons was strengthened in February when City scored a last-minute equaliser.

City's anxiety was reflected by a fourth-minute booking for Pring, cautioned after scything down Issa Kabore for the second time.

The gloom around Ashton Gate deepened when Worrall met Ben Whiteman's corner eight yards out and guided the ball inside the near post.

Home fans immediately responded to the goal with boos and directed cries of 'you're getting sacked in the morning' at Skubala.

Wrexham continued to press with Jacques Ekomie almost on the end of George Dobson's centre, and Bailey Cadamarteri smacking a post.

City slowly made their way back into the contest as Twine threatened and Jason Knight fired over.

But Whiteman showed wonderful technique to almost double Wrexham's lead, the midfielder getting over a bouncing ball from 25 yards to force Bradley Collins to tip over.

Twine flashed over, Dom Ballard headed wide, and Pring sent a shot into the side netting as City carved out half-chances.

The late flurry before the break did little to appease home fans who were quick to jeer off Skubala's side at the interval.

Within 50 seconds of the restart Anthony Paterson failed to find distance on his punch, and Ballard turned sharply to force a fine stop from the Wrexham goalkeeper.

It was a warning that Wrexham did not heed as George Thomason's heavy touch allowed Ballard to free Knight down the right.

Knight's cross made its way to the far post through a forest of legs and Pring arrived unmarked to find the bottom corner.

Patterson held Knight's spinning shot and then got his body behind a more powerful shot from the Robins' captain.

Wrexham went close eight minutes from time when Kieffer Moore broke away and fellow substitute Ollie Rathbone stuck a post.

"I really liked us second half. We looked more like the team I want it to be. To go 1-0 down so early was tough.

"You could see the lads were edgy, but we showed good character to come back against a good team.

"The way I want to play you have to be brave, and people forget we are still a new group working together.

"I've been in this situation many times before and at the back end of the season been very successful.

"I can see green shoots today I really liked. It's not a win but some really pleasing things in there."

"It was a very good first half, I was really pleased with the way we played. What we set out to do we executed really well.

"The second half in the first 10 minutes we made a lot of mistakes.

"We just needed to get through that period and come out the other side unscathed.

"They got the goal and we've got to look at ourselves in that moment.

"We needed a bit more composure, better decision-making and good game management, which we'd done in the first period.

"We clawed our way back and nearly went on to win it, but we'll take a point and four points from two games after winning at Lincoln on Saturday."

articles.title: La obra maestra de Jude: el inglés está 'on fire'
articles.standfirst: Bellingham marca uno de sus mejores goles en el Real Madrid para el delirio del Bernabéu
articles.summary: Bellingham marca uno de sus mejores goles en el Real Madrid para el delirio del Bernabéu
articles.body: Sonó el Hey Jude y más que nunca. No era para menos. Bellingham se inventó un gol con una volea que bien firmaría Zidane. Esta vez no bajó de cielo como en Hampden Park, esta vez se lo fabricó todo el inglés, que había salido tras el descanso para poner las cosas en su sitio. Un pequeño control para domar la pelota, otro con una especia de sombrero y un tercero con un golpe magistral con el exterior desde la frontal. Nada pudo hacer Kovar más que contemplar la obra de arte porque el balón era inalcanzable. Uno de los goles de la jornada, mejor dicho, va a ser uno de los goles de esta edición de la Champions. Mourinho movió con maestría el banquillo en busca de la remontada. Cambio de los dos centrales, Konaté y Huijsen al césped, y Bellingham, que había sido suplente para tomarse un descanso, por Tchouaméni. Bernardo Silva bajó metros e hizo más del francés mientras que el inglés se fue más arriba. Desde su salida, fue un recital, escoltado por la magia de Güler, todo hay que decirlo. El Madrid se empezó a mover y en un visto y o visto la cosa ya andaba 3-1. Ya no hay duda de que este es el Bellingham que deslumbró en su primera temporada en el Madrid. Deslumbró también con Inglaterra para romper la racha de la España de Luis de la Fuente, confirmando su juego excelso en el Madrid desde hace ya tiempo. Suma cinco goles y cuatro asistencias, pero el arreón viene desde hace poco. Dos goles en los tres últimos partidos de Liga, ante Racing y Celta, y dos en los dos últimos partidos de Champions. Ya pudo marcar Jude antes en un remate acrobático tras un gran pase de Mbappé, pero la pelota la sacó como pudo el portero del PSV. El inglés fue quien mejor vio las subidas de Valverde y con su empuje el equipo holandés se fue aculando atrás. La pelota se movía rápido, el Madrid ya jugaba a otra cosa. Luego llegó su golazo. Sus compañeros fueron no daban crédito mientras se acercaban a felicitarle. El gesto marca de la casa y el Madrid cantando el Hey Jude. Tuvo tiempo para meter de primeras un pase magistral a la carrera de Vini para que este hiciera el 5-1 definitivo. El inglés ha vuelto.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: Man Utd boss fumes at VAR in Liverpool loss over Leny Yoro and Dominik Szoboszlai calls
articles.summary: Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card in loss at Liverpool after call was overturned; Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino: "What were VAR doing?"; Poch also believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood
articles.body:
Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.

Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool.

It is the second time this season VAR has wrongly gone against Man Utd after ProRef admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford in September.

United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner, which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.

Pochettino mentioned the Haaland call in a passionate outburst over VAR as he questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.

"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.

"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?

"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.

"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way.

"We love and accept the technology, but what are they doing? But it's not only this mistake or the mistake for Haaland against Manchester City, it's how after it affects everything."

Poch explains why Szoboszlai goal shouldn't have stood

Pochettino then insisted that Liverpool's opening goal should not have stood because Bradley Barcola was touching the Manchester United wall as Szoboszlai struck in.

Pochettino referenced a similar call last season, which saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick goal for Crystal Palace at Chelsea disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.

The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1 m (1 yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."

Pochettino believes that the law applied to Szoboszlai's free-kick opener due to Barcola's involvement.

He said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years, they've maybe changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].

"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed.

"But this type of situation, I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say we were right and the decision wasn't good, and now the three points, where are they?

"I think it's a thing we need to think a little bit more deeper and it's not for tomorrow's game.

"It's about to be tough in the way we use the technology. We need to move on. I'm so proud of the players in the way they manage these unfair situations that happen on the field.

"Our focus now is to improve, to start to win games and tomorrow we have a great opportunity here."

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at ProRef, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.

Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR, John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.

Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.

"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

articles.title: Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Viktor Gyokeres goal cancelled out as Gunners frustrated in Champions League
articles.summary: Match report as Arsenal are denied victory by Borussia Dortmund in a Champions League encounter at the Emirates Stadium; Viktor Gyokeres scored a spectacular opener but Maximilian Beier equalised as the Gunners wasted a string of chances
articles.body:
Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal an early lead with a stunning strike from distance but the game followed a similar pattern to Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle as they were unable to capitalise on a one-sided first half before conceding after the break.

Dortmund's leveller came when Beier slotted a clinical finish past Kepa Arrizabalaga, standing in for the injured David Raya, following a rampaging run from defender Joane Gadou.

Arsenal racked up 30 shots and had a string of chances to win it in the closing stages, hitting the woodwork through Jurrien Timber's deflected cut-back and again through Declan Rice's low shot.

Gyokeres also spurned opportunities, firing over from close range from Martin Odegaard's pass shortly before half-time, then heading awkwardly wide from a few yards out when it looked easier to score from another Odegaard ball.

Dortmund had dangerous moments too, including a Jobe Bellingham goal ruled out for offside and a penalty appeal for a handball by Gyokeres following a corner.

Arsenal remain unbeaten in the Champions League but the draw causes them to drop two places in the league phase table to fifth before they resume their Premier League campaign at home to Manchester City, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

Arsenal fail to kill off another opponent

Arsenal's total of 30 shots was their highest in the Champions League either this season or last. But only one of them ended up in the net. Only four of them were even on target.

There were clear parallels with Saturday's game at St James' Park. Again, Arsenal were outstanding in the first half. Again, though, they reached the interval with only one goal to show for their efforts.

Dortmund, like Newcastle, came out with renewed belief, and a lot more intensity. Even before Beier's equaliser, the same player had missed a glorious chance when he failed to connect with a Joey Veerman cross. Arsenal were suddenly on the back foot.

They regained control after Dortmund's leveller, albeit while avoiding a scare when Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside. But their attempts to break down the visitors were unsuccessful. Good positions were wasted. They should have been out of sight.

Arteta couldn't believe it when the otherwise impressive Gyokeres skewed his header wide from Odegaard's cross. The Arsenal boss was on his knees when Timber's cut-back ricocheted off the post.

It is positive that they are creating so many chances. Their performance featured another bright showing from Noni Madueke. But they will need to find some cutting edge against City.

Arteta: Unbelievable we didn't score more

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta : "I think it was a brilliant performance.

"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today, is something to be very, very pleased about.

"There is very little more that you can demand from the team.

"But obviously there is the feeling that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, with the amount of chances and situations.

"There is an element of luck and there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

"I love the way the team played. I think there's no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game. It was great to watch.

"It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn't ended up in the back of the net. That's my feeling."

Kovac: VAR should have checked Gyokeres handball

Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac : "I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check.

"They are trying to intervene less, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.

"In such a situation, you have to at least have someone in the VAR room saying, 'Let's just look at it.'

"I am not crying about it. It is what it is. We got a point. It is a big point away to Arsenal, a big one for all of us, our fans, our team, and the club."

Arsenal's 30 shots is their highest total on record in a Champions League game (since 2003/04).

It is also the Gunners' most in a game that they failed to win across all competitions since December 2023 against West Ham, when they also had 30.

Arsenal have failed to win a home game in the group stage of major European competition for the first time since November 2019 (2-1 defeat vs Eintracht Frankfurt), ending a run of 18 successive victories - the longest such winning run by any side in major European competition history

articles.title: Michigan reportedly won't hire Texas A&M's Trev Alberts as its next athletic director
articles.summary: Alberts was set to succeed Warde Manuel with the Wolverines.
articles.body:
Trev Alberts won't be Michigan's next athletic director after all.

The school told the former Texas A&M athletic director that they would not hire him, according to multiple reports , including Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger. The decision comes after comments the athletic director made in a deposition from a lawsuit against Nebraska came to light.

In that deposition regarding a suit filed when he was Nebraska's athletic director, Albert said that "it depends" on if it would be OK for a coach to have a sexual relationship with an athlete. The testimony came after a former women's basketball player sued the school — including Alberts — after she had been dismissed from the team following her relationship with an assistant coach.

Incoming Michigan president C. Cybele Raver, who led the athletic director search, informed Michigan board members on Monday night that she had decided against the hiring of Alberts as it is "not in the best interest of the university," a source told Dellenger.

Since Alberts had signed a memorandum of understanding with the school, he will be owed his buyout. Alberts' attorney Tom Mars told Yahoo Sports there was no contingency language in the memorandum of understanding; Alberts was set to make approximately $4 million per season with the Wolverines and his buyout is just north of $17 million.

ESPN obtained a copy of the memorandum of understanding (MOU) on Tuesday. On the first page, it states that, pending the completion of the employment agreement, "this MOU shall form a binding contract" between Alberts and Michigan.

The MOU later details a notable buyout obligation. It declares that Michigan is responsible for paying Alberts' $4 million Texas A&M buyout to Texas A&M.

In a statement Tuesday , Alberts said that the interpretations of what he said in that deposition were an "egregious characterization of words taken out of context."

"The egregious characterization of words taken out of context from a deposition regarding an incident that occurred years ago is wrong and unfair," Alberts said. "I was informed that Michigan's General Counsel had spoken with the General Counsel of both Texas A&M and the University of Nebraska, as well as Nebraska's outside counsel, to inquire about the deposition. I was further told that all three of those lawyers told Michigan's GC that I had done nothing wrong or inappropriate and had followed all applicable university policies and procedures. I am proud of my long track record of standing up for student-athletes and for following the rules and my core values."

Michigan has been looking for a successor to outgoing athletic director Warde Manuel, who is stepping down at the end of the year. Manuel has been in charge during a tumultuous time in Michigan athletics as multiple scandals have enveloped the football program in recent years.

"The University of Michigan's search for its next athletic director is ongoing," the school said in a statement Tuesday. "As we navigate a rapidly changing landscape in intercollegiate athletics, the values that define Michigan will guide our decisions and reinforce our commitment to excellence and integrity, both in the classroom and in competition. "

In a letter to Alberts announcing the decision , Raver and outgoing school president Dominic Grasso said that the school "has determined that the background check is not acceptable to the University."

"Therefore, the University will not complete the negotiation and execution of an employment agreement as provided for in the MOU executed by the parties. In addition, the information gathered in the background check provides good cause to terminate the MOU between the parties. Any offer of potential employment is immediately withdrawn and negotiations are terminated."

Alberts has already resigned from Texas A&M with his departure scheduled for Nov. 30. His hire falling through at Michigan could also directly impact the football program's future. Kyle Whittingham's status beyond the 2026 season has been in question because of the Wolverines' struggles this season.

Hiring an athletic director was seen as a potential first step toward figuring out if Whittingham or someone else would lead the program in 2027.

Instead, Michigan is back to not having an athletic director in place for 2027 with one week left in the regular season. Michigan (6-5) did get bowl-eligible in Week 12 with an upset win over previously undefeated UCLA.

Alberts, a former Nebraska linebacker, was the athletic director at Nebraska for over three years before heading to Texas A&M in 2024. While he was in charge in Lincoln, former women's basketball player Ashley Scoggin sued the school's board of regents, former assistant coach Chuck Love and Alberts after she claimed she was groomed by Love as part of a secret relationship with him.

When Alberts was deposed in December 2025, he did not unequivocally say it would be problematic for a coach to have a relationship with a player. From USA Today:

Over a pair of depositions that lasted about seven hours combined, Alberts was asked by one of Scoggin's attorneys, Maren Chaloupka, if he believed college coaches should never have sex with athletes, especially since the university had a policy forbidding relationships between faculty and students, a rule that included coaches. Alberts responded that he "didn't know the answer to that" and then said "it depends" and there was "nuance" since eligibility rules following the COVID-19 pandemic meant some students were "25, 26 years old," and some of the coaches could be "27, 28." "Clearly, if there is a — if there is an assumption or if we think that's happening, that's when we are not encouraged, but trained to report it to the experts," Alberts said in the deposition . "We are not experts in this. I'm not an expert in that area. And I don't make that judgment."

articles.title: Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
articles.summary: Arsenal dominate the chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back for a 1-1 draw in football’s Champions League.
articles.body:
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres showed why he is such a polarising figure with a thunderous goal and a crucial miss in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Swedish striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at London’s Emirates Stadium.

Initially, Gyokeres looked like he was doing just that with his first goal at Emirates this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions.

But the 28-year-old has been much maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025.

And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages.

Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier by then, and Arteta was left to rue his decision to put his faith in Gyokeres.

Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season.

In a showdown between the current leaders of the Premier League and the Bundesliga, Arsenal were too profligate in attack and error-prone at the back to say they deserved all three points.

Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them.

Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday.

Arsenal were in control at the start, and Christos Tzolis’s strike bounced just over before Gyokeres tested Dortmund keeper Gregor Kobel with a long-range drive.

It was a warning Dortmund failed to heed as Gyokeres put Arsenal ahead in the 10th minute.

Fatally backing off when Gyokeres took possession 25 yards from goal, Dortmund’s defenders were punished by the Swede as he unleashed a superb dipping strike that flashed into the roof of the net.

Arsenal’s luck runs out in Champions League

Tzolis nearly doubled Arsenal’s lead with a curler that forced a sprawling save from Kobel.

Declan Rice almost replicated Gyokeres’s goal with a ferocious blast that fizzed just over.

Kepa Arrizabalaga was deputising for David Raya in goal for Arsenal after his fellow Spaniard suffered a shoulder injury in Saturday’s draw at Newcastle.

Such was Arsenal’s dominance that Kepa did not make a save until the final minute of the first half when he blocked Joane Gadou’s shot at the near post.

But Dortmund have a well-earned reputation as a stronger team in the second half this season, and they lived up to that tag once again.

Dortmund had a strong penalty appeal rejected after Gyokeres blocked a corner with his arm.

And with Arsenal unusually sloppy at the back, Dortmund’s pressure was rewarded in the 55th minute.

Gadou surged towards the Arsenal area before slipping a pass into Beier, who eluded Gabriel Magalhaes to plant a clinical low finish past Kepa.

Kobel saved Piero Hincapie’s close-range header as Arsenal tried to respond, while Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham had a goal disallowed for a tight offside.

Gyokeres wasted his chance to finish as Arsenal’s hero for once when he sent a close-range diving header woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross.

Arsenal’s luck was out after Odegaard’s delivery twice hit the post and appeared to strike Serhou Guirassy’s hand before it was finally scrambled clear.

Rice was equally unfortunate with a first-time drive that cannoned back off the near post to leave Arsenal frustrated.

articles.summary: El centrocampista atendió a la prensa en la zona mixta del Bernabéu
articles.body: Jude Bellingham atendió a los medios de comunicación en la zona mixta del Santiago Bernabéu después de la victoria del Real Madrid ante el PSV. El inglés, autor de uno de los goles de la noche, repasó su gran momento de forma, la influencia de José Mourinho en su rendimiento, la situación de Vinicius y la posibilidad de renovar su contrato con el conjunto blanco. Golazo: "Sí, ha sido bueno. He recibido el balón y he pensado: 'no voy a pasar, voy a tirar y ha sido gol. Gol muy bonito y por eso soy muy feliz". Mejor momento de tu carrera: "Puede ser. Estoy disfrutando mucho mi fútbol. Me encanta el entrenador, su staff, mis compañeros. Me ayudan mucho. Por eso estoy jugando bien, porque tengo mucha ayuda de todo el equipo". La influencia de Mourinho y su posición en el campo: "No sé si es porque estoy jugando de mediapunta. Yo creo que es la diversidad, para jugar más bajo, para ayudar en la construcción del juego. Me voy un poco más alto para finalizar. Yo creo que Mourinho me da mucha confianza. Sí, por eso estoy jugando bien, porque estoy feliz". Mourinho, la clave de su mejoría: "Mourinho... y punto". Vinicius y el apoyo del vestuario: "Sí, porque es un chico maravilloso, un jugador maravilloso. Me encanta cómo juega, pero me encanta más cómo es como persona. Yo creo que vosotros lo atacáis mucho, porque es un jugador un poco, no sé, split opinion (opiniones divididas). Yo creo que él necesita ayuda de sus compañeros, por eso estamos aquí para él siempre y estoy muy feliz". El margen de mejora del equipo: "Sí, es siempre importante mejorar. Pienso en cómo hacemos mejor en el próximo partido. No es suficiente solo ganar, ganar, ganar. Estamos siempre aprendiendo más sobre cómo jugar mejor y por eso estamos ganando, porque estamos aprendiendo". La posibilidad de ser capitán del Real Madrid: "No sé, tenemos capitanes muy buenos ya, tipo Fede, Vini, Rodrygo, los chicos que han hecho muchas temporadas aquí. Estoy muy bien en mi posición, aprendiendo cosas, mejorando mi español un poco y sí, estoy aprendiendo mucho de mis compañeros". La charla de Mourinho en el descanso: "Sí, un poco enfadado, pero es normal, es un entrenador con mucho nivel y espera mucho más de nosotros y yo creo que en la segunda parte hemos mejorado mucho más". Su posible renovación: "Honestamente no he hablado con el club sobre renovación, he visto en las redes sociales y he hablado con mi madre y mi padre y les he dicho: '¿Esto es verdad o no?'. Estoy feliz aquí, estoy jugando bien, disfrutando mi fútbol, me encanta vivir aquí en España, para mí todo es perfecto en este club ahora mismo y contrato, renovaciones, en un tiempo más largo". Superar a Zidane y Beckham en goles: "Feliz siempre porque son mis ídolos, Zidane, Beckham, McManaman, todos estos son ídolos para mí, es un placer jugar en este club con la historia que tenemos aquí".

articles.standfirst: La estrella del Betis refleja el estado de optimismo del equipo en las tres competiciones
articles.summary: La estrella del Betis refleja el estado de optimismo del equipo en las tres competiciones
articles.body: isco Alarcón, que puso con música el segundo gol en la cabeza del Cucho para rematar el partido contra el Slovan, aseguró al terminar el encuentro que el 'top 8' está en el objetivo del equipo, cuarto en estos momentos tras las cinco primeras jornadas de la fase liga. "Hay que hacerle caso al ingeniero, y si dice que esto no es nada, que hay que ir a por el 'top 8' pues vamos a intentarlo, veremos a ver, vienen grandes rivales (Como, Bayern, Arsenal...) y a ver si lo conseguimos. Por eso hoy nos jugábamos mucho, por lo que nos viene, y la mentalidad es la de ir a por todas contra equipos a los que les gusta mucho el fútbol. ¿El derbi? Ya está olvidado, no te puedes recrear, pasa rápido y hay que pensar en el siguiente partido, ya hemos hecho autocrítica porque somos los primeros que queremos mejorar", aseguró la estrella del Betis "La labor del míster es fundamental en este momento, son tres competiciones, rota, da descansos, hace que todos estén enchufados sin que te toque jugar sin tener minutos previos, y es clave si queremos hacer una buena temporada, porque la exigencia de la Champions no es la de la Europa League o la Conference, y la clave es todos pensar que estamos ahí, que podemos jugar y ojalá dure toda la temporada". Isco fue clave en la victoria y en lograr darle la vuelta al partido desde el frío arranque de la primera parte. "Muy contento por la victoria, no era fácil, el campo no estaba bien, pero nos hemos adaptado aunque no entramos bien, en el final de la primera y toda la segunda hemos estado muy bien, nos merecíamos la victoria". Y el Cucho, vital: "Contento por el Cucho, lo conocemos, trabaja mucho y nos da mucho más que solo goles, se lo merece más allá de los goles, estamos todos enchufados y es una buena señal del equipo que tengamos a todos así porque esto dura mucho y es vital".

articles.title: Vinicius agradece el abrazo de sus compañeros: "¡Somos una familia!"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño, autor del 5-1, arropado por el resto del equipo tras su gol
articles.summary: El brasileño, autor del 5-1, arropado por el resto del equipo tras su gol
articles.body: Vinicius marcó el 5-1 del Real Madrid ante el PSV y, de repente, una lluvia de brazos le sepultó. Sus compañeros se lanzaron a por él, Mbappé llamó hasta a los centrales para que acudieran y, una vez todos en la piña, empezaron a botar para animar al brasileño. "Muy feliz por cómo mis compañeros han celebrado un gol que necesitaba. ¡Somos una familia! Muchas gracias de verdad. ¡Os quiero mucho! ¡A por más!", escribió Vini en Instagram tras el encuentro. Ese "un gol que necesitaba" deja claro que Vinicius no lo ha pasado bien. Que ha tenido unas semanas difíciles. Su sanción de cuatro partidos le mandó a un segundo plano del que no consiguió salir en los encuentros de Champions en los que sí podía jugar. El runrún del Bernabéu, sus malas actuaciones y los cambios tempranos de Mourinho han hecho mella en un jugador que no encuentra su nivel desde hace demasiado tiempo y que necesita un impulso para revertir su situación. En la tarea se han implicado también sus compañeros, que quieren recuperar a Vini en el plano emocional para que la mejoría en el fútbol venga después. Mbappé le buscó en el gol, le regaló su MVP y lideró un abrazo que puede ser medicina para el brasileño.

articles.title: Man City 2-2 Napoli: Enzo Maresca's side grinding to a halt
articles.summary: Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt, as displayed in their laborious Champions League draw against Napoli.
articles.body:
Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt.

The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.

It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.

Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.

City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.

Maresca said: "We are always looking for three points but when you are not able to win it is important you that don't lose. We take the point, five games [played],10 points and overall I think it is a good result in the end.

"Today, off the ball, once again we didn't concede a lot, the problem is that in this moment they are clinical when we concede a chance, almost every time it is finishing with a goal. We created many chances but in this moment it is like this and move on.

"The first 10 games we always scored first and then in this moment it is exactly in the opposite way, we just need to find a way to avoid that, but I don't think it affects the players in terms of their confidence. We fought until the end."

Cherki rescues point for Man City against Napoli

City were strong favourites for this game and should have had few issues in collecting all three points against a Napoli side that are languishing in eighth place in Serie A.

Their injury issues mean they were able to name only seven substitutes, two of those being goalkeepers, while they had suffered defeat in their past three meetings with City.

They threatened a shock result after twice going ahead through well-taken goals from Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, but Rayan Cherki managed to salvage a late draw for the hosts.

Maresca's side had 62.7% possession and attempted 665 passes, which largely lacked incisiveness, and of that figure 303 were in the final third compared to Napoli's 77.

The latest disappointing result means City's perfect start is quickly unravelling, now having won only one of their past seven games in all competitions inside 90 minutes.

"It was really surprising to see Manchester City so dull in the first half and so predictable," former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"If you play a team that takes their time, you get yourself set. It is 100% easier to defend.

"You sit and watch City pass, pass, pass, slow, slow. You can get a cigar out."

Star striker Erling Haaland has been in prolific form again this season, scoring 20 goals for club and country, but the 26-year-old has drawn a blank in his past two games.

The Norwegian had chances but failed to score against Fulham on Saturday and though he was handed the captain's armband against Napoli, Haaland was on the periphery for much of the game.

The frontman managed only 14 touches of the ball against the Serie A side on Tuesday, the lowest figure of any player that started the match.

It raises the question whether he is receiving the service to try and find the back of the net.

"I feel I am getting more than enough chances to score," Haaland told TNT Sports. "We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't. Not good enough and we let them in too easy.

"Football is easy and difficult; when you win it's easy and you know what to do, when you don't you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy."

City are sixth in the Champions League table, before Wednesday's games, but in the Premier League they have failed to win their past four.

It does not get any easier this weekend, facing a daunting trip to leaders Arsenal on Sunday as they aim to find some form.

Haaland added: "It's the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away.

"We need a top performance from every single player."

articles.title: Jude Bellingham: Real Madrid midfielder plays down Zinedine Zidane comparison after wonder goal
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho says Jude Bellingham is the best midfielder in the world, but the Real Madrid star played down comparisons to Zinedine Zidane.
articles.body:
Manager Jose Mourinho described Jude Bellingham as "without any doubt, the best midfielder in the world" following a wonder goal which inspired a brilliant second-half performance for Real Madrid in a 5-1 win against PSV .

Mourinho opted to leave the England midfielder out of the starting line-up for Tuesday's Champions League game at the Bernabeu - an understandable decision given the demands of Madrid's fixture schedule and the strength in depth at his disposal.

But after watching his side trail 1-0 at half-time against the Dutch side, Mourinho knew changes were needed.

"He is an amazing player that has everything," the Portuguese manager said. "He has physicality, he understands the game, he has absolutely everything. Today, he has changed how the game was evolving."

Captain Fede Valverde equalised in the 50th minute and 10 minutes later Bellingham produced his moment of magic.

Receiving the ball just outside the penalty area, he took two touches to lift it into position before unleashing a magnificent volley with the outside of his right footr, leaving PSV keeper Matej Kovar with no chance.

It was a sensational finish, executed with extraordinary precision.

"I was a bit surprised, honestly," Bellingham said about the goal. "I knew that I could control the ball well and get it into my grasp. But normally from there, I'm looking to see who's on as an option to play through.

"It popped up nicely and I thought I'm just going to hit it. So yeah, it was a nice goal and important for the team, being the second goal, and gave us control."

The 23-year-old celebrated in trademark fashion, standing with his arms outstretched in front of the home supporters as thousands serenaded him with chants of 'Hey Jude'.

It was his fourth goal in his past five appearances for Real.

Asked whether he should be compared to Real and France legend Zinedine Zidane, who won the Ballon d'Or and World Cup in 1998, Bellingham maintained his humility.

"I think Zidane is much better than me. He's much more elegant and he's my idol," he said.

Kylian Mbappe scored two more goals and Vinicius Junior put away the fifth to complete a super turnaround from a team that had looked short of ideas in the first half.

At the suggestion that he is currently in the form of his life, Bellingham said: "I think you're only as good as your next one [game]. Your last one doesn't really matter.

"But my focus has to change now to preparing for the next game. Thinking about my best form or being the best player in the world doesn't mean anything to me."

For Bellingham, the ability to respond when things are not going according to plan is what separates the best teams from the rest.

"We're managing to show that mentality that good teams do, that even if you're not playing well, you can raise the level at any point," he said.

His adaptation to life in Spain has also been an important part of that journey.

Asked about his increasingly impressive Spanish, Bellingham admitted he still gets nervous when speaking the language in public.

"It's getting a little bit better. I get a little bit nervous speaking to you guys. It's much easier in the changing room," he joked to journalists.

"I'm loving living in Spain. I'm loving the club. I think for English players it's such an important thing to go and move abroad and learn new things and I've obviously benefited massively from that."

And while his performances have inevitably brought renewed attention to individual awards, Bellingham said that personal recognition is not what motivates him.

Asked about the Ballon d'Or, he said his focus was only on the team.

"I don't care about the Ballon d'Or, honestly. I want to win a lot of titles with the team, the Champions League, the League."

"The Ballon d'Or is something for you, journalists, to vote and create a bit of tension. But for me it's more important that the team win."

articles.title: Rangers Goalkeeper Ivor Pandur Outlines Croatia Ambitions
articles.summary: In a recent interview with the Scottish media, Rangers number one goalkeeper Ivor Pandur has been honest about his ambitions to become the long term number o...
articles.body:
In the summer transfer window, Rangers made the move to sign Croatian goalkeeper Ivor Pandur from recently promoted Premier League side, Hull City.

The 26-year old has been an important part of Hull's unlikely promotion from the Championship. Their underlying numbers were very poor, and were therefore reliant on individual quality at both ends of the pitch, and he certainly ticked one of those boxes with his excellent performances.

Since moving north of the border, Pandur has continued to impress and appears to have the approval of the Rangers fanbase as well as those within the Scottish media. So far, so good.

Back in the summer, he was named in Croatia's squad for the FIFA World Cup in the USA, Canada and Mexico, having also been involved in their two most previous squads before the tournament, as well as the two since.

However, despite clearly being a regular member of the squad, Pandur has yet to make his debut for the Croatia national team, neither under former manager Zlatko Dalic, nor his successor, the returning Slaven Bilic.

Well, he has admitted that he hopes that soon changes, as he outlined his ambitions of becoming Croatia number one in a recent interview with STV News , saying that his move to the club could be the catalyst for that: "That's why I came here, knowing how big this club is, and the stage, and the following.

But I always just need to focus on myself and my work. Hopefully it will make me Croatian number one soon enough. That's one of my goals, but I'm focused on giving my best every day. Hopefully that will be enough for me to take over."

Some positive comments from Pandur, and you can't see why he can't one day be the number one. Interestingly, Bilic recently said that the national team keepers must be playing at their clubs, and current number one, Dominik Livakovic is currently the number two keeper at Barcelona. Which is still pretty good, but it means he is not playing every single week.

So, perhaps there will be a role available soon for the Rangers goalkeeper. Croatia will play the Republic of Ireland in a two legged promotion/relegation UEFA Nations League play-off at the end of March. The winner will be in League A for the next iteration of the tournament. Perhaps that will provide a debut for Pandur, but it is still a while away yet, so let's see.

articles.title: Post Match Reactions: Dortmund escape with a point
articles.summary: Physically and mentally grueling. That’s what typically exemplifies a match against Arsenal. Tuesday was no different for Borussia Dortmund. BVB traveled to...
articles.body:
Physically and mentally grueling. That's what typically exemplifies a match against Arsenal. Tuesday was no different for Borussia Dortmund.

BVB traveled to the Emirates to face the North London side in the Champions League. Both teams came into the match mirroring each other across their respective domestic leagues in terms of goals scored (17), goals conceded (seven), and place in the standings (1st).

And both teams left with a point a piece, as Dortmund and Arsenal fought to a 1-1 tie.

From the opening whistle, Arsenal dictated the game. Which lead to the opener from Viktor Gyökeres. The Swede unleashed a missile from long-range – only his third goal of the season across all competitions. Gregor Kobel's positioning could have been better, and Nico Schlotterbeck should have stepped up instead of backing off. But with a shot like that, with as much venom and top spin that was behind it, sometimes you just have to tip your cap.

The Gunners had several other chances throughout the rest of the first half. The most notable came in the 35th minute when Declan Rice was nearly clean through on goal. Schlotterbeck made up ground and with his out stretched leg blocked Rice's shot from around the 18 yard line, denying the english midfield engine an excellent chance on goal.

The second half saw BVB much more aggressive not only in their pressing but in their possession. Joane Gadou was one of the more menacing attacking players (huh!?). The right centerback back had a cross/shot in the first half that Kepa Arrizabalaga was able to parry away with ease. And in the second half, Gadou provided the assist to Dortmund's lone goal in the 55th minute. Starting from BVB's defensive half, the frenchman drove through Arsenal's press, like a determined UPS driver around the holidays, before laying off a package of a pass to Maximilian Beier, who did nice work to cut back inside, beating Kepa at his near post.

For the first 15-20 minutes of the second half, Dortmund were able to maintain possession, and more importantly were able to win the ball back after losing it. In the 68th minute Jobe Bellingham scored what appeared to be the go-ahead goal, after a rebound from a great Joey Veerman shot. But Bellingham was narrowly called offside.

From that wakeup call, Arsenal grew back into the game, with the hosts seemingly throwing barrage after barrage at BVB. The Premier League champions had 30 total shots. But only four of them were on target (same as Dortmund).

Regardless, Niko Kovač's side battled from down a goal to earn a draw against one of the best teams in the world, and with that, sit in the seventh spot in the Champions League standings.

Waldemar Anton struggled mightily against Gyökeres. The Swede constantly got the better of Anton. The main thing that concerned me was Anton's indecisiveness. He seemed to hesitate throughout the night on when to attack the ball or not. This lead to him getting blown by multiple times.

I understand Kovač wanting to bring on Konstantinos Karetsas, but felt that throwing him on in place of Beier wasn't the right decision. Beier provided the best attacking threat for the visitors throughout the night. The timing of the decision was also puzzling, considering it came only nine minutes after he leveled things up for Dortmund. They had momentum, but not long after the sub was made was when Arsenal started taking control back of the match.

Roughly 3,000 BVB away fans made the trek to London. They were loud, wavering their yellow and black scarves on and off throughout the match. In what's become one of Europe's most difficult fortresses to play in, it was awesome to see the BVB supporters help will the black and yellow to a solid result.

What did you think of the match? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Charles Huff: “I will be the head coach at the University of Memphis next year”
articles.summary: Charles Huff shuts down coaching carousel rumors, confirms commitment to Memphis.
articles.body:
Late November is when the college football coaching carousel typically begins to spin. Dozens of coaches are dismissed, vacancies emerge, and speculation swirls about potential replacements. It's a chaotic time for head coaches, especially those still jockeying for spots in conference championship games or the College Football Playoff.

But Memphis head coach Charles Huff isn't interested in becoming part of the carousel.

During his Tuesday media availability, Huff was asked about his interest in the Maryland head coaching vacancy. The first-year Tigers coach responded with an unusually definitive message, addressing the rumors head-on.

"I typically don't address these things publicly because I would be addressing every opening and every rumor and every podcast every week and it would be more about Coach Huff than the Memphis Tigers," Huff said. "I have not interviewed for Maryland. I will not interview for Maryland."

Then, Huff followed with a message of reassurance to the Memphis faithful.

"I will be the head coach at the University of Memphis next year," Huff confirmed. "(Athletic director) Dr. Ed Scott, (President) Dr. (Bill) Hardgrave have known that since about a month ago. I told them when all of the rumbling started with everything — not just Maryland — that I wasn't taking any jobs this year. I wasn't taking any interviews. I told my representation a month and a half ago I'm not interested in the job cycle."

Huff further elaborated on his commitment to Memphis, confirming that the Tigers already resigned several players for next season.

"I committed to Memphis," Huff said. "I committed to Dr. Scott. We've already started talking about improvements for next year holistically in the program. Dr. Scott and I meet every week and we've talked about some things. We've already got 10 to 15 players resigned for next year. Once you sign, you can't transfer, so it would be really, really hard to resign them and then try to go somewhere else."

Huff's coaching journey has involved three stops in three years. He spent 2021-24 as the head coach of Marshall, capturing the Sun Belt title in his final season. After the two parties could not reach an agreement on an extension, Huff departed for fellow Sun Belt program Southern Miss. He spent one season with the Golden Eagles before accepting the Memphis job, where he has quickly developed appreciation for his new home.

"I was told when I got here that if I love Memphis, it would love me back," Huff said. "That's what I've tried to do. That's what I feel from this city. The reason I'm addressing it is because I do think the noise is getting a little loud. Just like I tell my players, sometimes you got to turn it off. And the reality of it is, hopefully now everyone can go to lunch at their job and focus on Temple, and how do we get to the game to support these players for Temple?"

Memphis (8-3, 5-2 American) approaches its regular season finale against Temple, and the stakes are high for the Tigers. With a victory, Memphis could position for its first American Conference Championship Game appearance since 2019. The Tigers currently sit in a three-way tie for second place in the American standings with North Texas and East Carolina, one game behind conference leader UTSA. Many potential tiebreaker scenarios involving the Tigers ultimately come down to computer rankings, making the final weekend especially consequential.

Tigers fans can breathe easier heading into Saturday's matchup against Temple, knowing that their head coach is focused on delivering a long-awaited championship and building Memphis for the future.

"Hopefully everyone can take a deep breath now or throw darts at my arm instead of my head and get out and support these guys," Huff said. "Everybody just focus on Temple, Temple, Temple, Temple, Temple, Temple, Temple. How do we fill the stadium for Temple? How do we make sure on third down it's extremely loud so they can't communicate? How do we show these 25 seniors that we appreciate what they've done this season? How do we show this team that we understand that this is an unbelievable opportunity, not just for the team, not just for our community, but for everybody? We have a chance to do something that hasn't been done since 2019, and that to me is special."

articles.title: Why Wyoming suspended head coach for regular season finale game vs. UConn
articles.summary: The Wyoming Cowboys are bowl-eligible this season as they enter Week 13 with a 7-4 record. However, the program will have to play the regular-season finale a...
articles.body:
The Wyoming Cowboys are bowl-eligible this season as they enter Week 13 with a 7-4 record. However, the program will have to play the regular-season finale against the UConn Huskies without its head coach, as Jay Sawvel will serve a suspension for that contest.

Reports indicate that the 55-year-old is serving a "self-imposed" suspension after revealing he tampered with student-athletes in December 2025, according to Chris Vannini of The Athletic. It's said that seven student-athletes were allegedly involved in the tampering and announced their intention to transfer to Wyoming before officially entering the transfer portal.

"The University of Wyoming has worked collaboratively with the NCAA Enforcement staff and self-imposed a one-game suspension for Head Football Coach Jay Sawvel for the game against the University of Connecticut on November 28, 2026, in response to NCAA rules violations related to impermissible communication with prospective student-athletes and their representatives last December (2025)," the University said in a statement.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"The seven involved student-athletes were enrolled at other NCAA member institutions, had publicly announced (via social media) their intention to transfer, but had not yet entered the NCAA transfer portal. Consistent with NCAA rules, Wyoming self-reported these violations, which have been classified as Level II-mitigated," Wyoming continued in the statement. "The matter is being resolved through the negotiated resolution process."

Wyoming will play Saturday's contest with defensive ends coach Brian Hendricks filling in as the interim head coach against UConn. Sawvel's suspension comes at a crucial time, as the Cowboys are still in contention to clinch a spot in the Mountain West Conference Championship. The team is scheduled to kick off against UConn on Saturday, November 28, at 12 p.m. EST.
